context: Your firm received cash in advance for IT services to be performed in the future.
question: Can you recognize revenue NOW?
option_b: No — performance obligation not yet satisfied
option_c: Yes — if the contract is signed
explanation: Revenue requires (1) work is done and (2) collection is probable. Cash was received but NO work has been performed yet — the performance obligation has not been satisfied. No revenue.

context: You sold inventory on account to a good creditworthy customer. You delivered the goods.
question: Can you recognize revenue NOW?
option_b: Yes — goods delivered and collection is probable
explanation: On account means no cash yet but that is okay. The performance obligation (deliver the good) IS satisfied and it is probable you will collect from a good customer. Full revenue recognized now.

context: You completed building a bridge and have only been paid 50% so far. The remaining 50% is owed by a financially strong government client.
question: How much revenue can you recognize?
option_c: 100% — work is done and collection is probable
explanation: 100%. The work IS done (performance obligation satisfied) and it IS probable you will collect the remaining 50% from a strong government client. Both conditions are met — recognize 100%.

context: Your firm received rent payment on September 1st for September rent.
question: How much revenue can you recognize on September 1st?
option_a: All of Septembers rent — cash was received
option_b: None — no time has passed yet
option_c: Half — you are partway through the month
explanation: On September 1st zero time has passed. The performance obligation (allowing tenant use of the asset) is satisfied only as time passes. No revenue on September 1st — even if it is non-refundable.

context: You sold inventory on account to a customer who is a bad credit risk — only 40% likely to pay.
question: Can you recognize revenue NOW?
option_c: Yes but only 40% of the amount
explanation: Collection must be PROBABLE to recognize revenue. At only 40% likelihood collection is not probable. No revenue until either (a) they pay or (b) their creditworthiness improves to probable.

context: You have a government contract to repair roads over 6 years. You are 1 year (1/6) complete. Collection is probable.
question: How much revenue can you recognize after Year 1?
explanation: Long-term contracts use the percentage-of-completion method. You have completed 1/6 and collection is probable — recognize 1/6 of total contract revenue in Year 1. Waiting until Year 6 would misrepresent what happened.

context: Costco receives a full years membership fee ($65) from a customer on July 1st.
question: How much revenue can Costco recognize on July 1st?
explanation: On July 1st no time has passed under the membership. The performance obligation is satisfied over 12 months. Costco recognizes $0 on July 1st then recognizes 1/12 each month as time passes (~$5.42/month).
